program: Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) — City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD), administered by SomerCor 504, Inc. Program Rules updated January 2026. TIF-funded reimbursement grant for permanent building improvements in designated TIF districts.
eligibility:
Gates (all verified from live SomerCor/DPD Program Rules, Jan 2026 and the live application form):
1. PROPERTY LOCATION: project must sit inside a TIF district that has SBIF authorized and currently open for applications (check via SBIF Locator Tool / rollout calendar). LaSalle Central has its own special rule set (below).
2. APPLICANT TYPE (mutually exclusive, selected on form): Commercial Owner, Commercial Tenant, Commercial Multi-Tenant, Commercial Landlord, Industrial Owner, Industrial Tenant, Industrial Multi-Tenant, Industrial Landlord, Non-Profit Owner, Non-Profit Tenant.
3. SIZE/FINANCIAL THRESHOLDS (determine both eligibility and reimbursement %):
   - Commercial business (owner-occupied or tenant): average annual gross sales < $9,000,000 over past 3 years (or 3-year projection for start-ups/business plan).
   - Industrial business: ≤200 full-time-equivalent employees.
   - Landlord/property owner (no ownership interest in occupying business): net worth ≤ $9,000,000 AND liquid assets ≤ $500,000 per individual/entity.
   - Tenant: must meet Annual Sales Requirement AND hold a leasehold interest AND have express prior property-owner approval for the specific improvements.
   - Reimbursement % tiers (commercial, by sales or net worth): <$3M = 90%; $3-6M = 60%; $6-9M = 30%. Industrial: flat 50% regardless of size (up to the 200-employee cap).
4. SITE CONTROL: deed or executed lease agreement, required by the Stage 1 deadline.
5. NOT a national chain/franchise (per DPD definition) — disqualifying, no exception.
6. NOT an ineligible use type: branch banks, day-labor/employment agencies, currency exchanges, payday/title loan or pawn shops, fortune-telling services, liquor stores, taverns/bars (unless licensed 2+ calendar years — see special tavern rule), hotels/motels, adult uses, private clubs, nationally-affiliated not-for-profits, start-up banquet halls (<1 year in business), track wagering, K-12 schools, gas stations, firearms dealers/ranges, places of worship (unless religious org runs a qualifying business — special affidavit rule), smoke shops/tobacco dealers, residential storage/trailer-storage/junk yards, government-owned/leased property (City, CHA, CPS, etc.).
7. NO disqualifying legal status: no Lis Pendens, pending litigation, code enforcement action, injunctions, foreclosure actions, or liens (mechanic's/tax/judgment) against the property or title.
8. City-debt / scofflaw clearance: applicant (and, if <7.5% single owner, ALL owners/entities) must not be indebted to the City (parking tickets, water bills, license fees) — a payment plan is acceptable if in current compliance — and must be in compliance with child-support laws (verified via full SSN through SomerCor's secure portal).
9. Current on Cook County property taxes — required at both the commitment-letter stage AND before final reimbursement.
10. City-employee/elected-official cap: no more than $1,000/calendar year in aggregate City loan/grant assistance unless specifically designated exempt.
11. Property-level cooldown: a given "Property" (single building, or contiguous commonly-owned parcels ≥7.5% common ownership) can only receive Maximum Program Assistance once every 3 years; after receiving the max, must wait 3 years from final payment before reapplying for that property.
12. Offset rule: max grant reduced dollar-for-dollar by any other "Direct City Financial Assistance" (e.g., Neighborhood Opportunity Fund, Community Development Grant) received, committed, or currently being provided for that property within 3 years of application.
13. Vacant-property rule: if the property is vacant, reimbursement requires 100% lease-up of the SBIF-funded portion by a qualified, actively operating tenant, evidenced by an executed lease.
14. LaSalle Central TIF special rules: max $250,000/project, $1,000,000/property; up to 90% reimbursement; no net worth/liquidity/sales caps; ground-floor improvements only (upper/lower floors at DPD discretion); +$50,000 bonus for businesses expanding from a Qualifying Low-/Moderate-Income Neighborhood; no other Direct City Financial Assistance to the property in the same 3-year window.
15. DPD holds sole, final discretion to deny applications based on past misrepresentation/non-compliance, and can remove a project mid-stream for major changes (e.g., altered construction plans, damage, or start-up business-plan changes).

timelineNotes:
Funding windows open per TIF district on a fixed monthly rotating calendar (verified live, 2026 schedule): July = Archer/Western, Lawrence/Kedzie, Lincoln Avenue, Little Village Industrial, Washington Park. August = 43rd/Cottage Grove, Clark/Montrose, Goose Island, Northwest Industrial Corridor, West Woodlawn. September = 107th/Halsted, Fullerton/Milwaukee, LaSalle Central, Madison/Austin, Woodlawn. October = Englewood Neighborhood, Greater Southwest (East), Pilsen Industrial Corridor, South Chicago, Stevenson/Brighton. November = Lawrence/Broadway, Little Village East, Midwest, Pulaski Corridor, Stockyards Southeast Quadrant. December = 111th/Kedzie, Austin Commercial, Bronzeville, Division/Homan, Touhy/Western. Each window runs from the 1st at 9:00 AM through the 30th at 5:00 PM (verify current month's list live each cycle — rollout calendars shift year to year).

PREPARABLE BEFORE A WINDOW OPENS (foundational/continuity-of-effort work): confirming TIF district and ward via the locator tool; legal business name, DBA, entity/ownership structure, formation date, industry description; whether business is a start-up/chain/franchise (disqualifying checks); other-location list; site-control documentation (deed or lease) gathered/organized; 3 years of tax returns, income statements, and bank statements assembled for net-worth/sales verification; start-up business plan and 36-month projections if applicable; property tax good-standing check; scofflaw/child-support self-check (SSNs are only submitted once SomerCor requests them, but compliance status can be checked ahead); rough project scope/description and a "best guess" budget table (contractor estimates NOT required at initial application — the form explicitly allows a good-faith estimate); prior/pending City financial assistance history (NOF, CDG, TIF, previous SBIF) for the offset-rule disclosure.

MUST WAIT for a program-specific step (cannot be done in advance): the initial application itself can only be submitted during the property's TIF district's specific monthly window; the Stage 1 coordinator's specific document request (varies by applicant type, sets the 20-day clock); the 2 competing licensed-contractor bids (Stage 2, needs SomerCor's go-ahead and a defined scope after Stage 1 review); the Conditional Commitment Letter (construction may not legally begin before this is issued — starting early makes those costs ineligible for reimbursement); permit applications tied to the approved scope (should be filed "immediately upon receiving SBIF approval," within the 120-day Stage 3.4 window); proof-of-financing showing 50% of contract price (tied to the approved contract price, which is only known after bids are in); all Stage 4 proof-of-payment documents (necessarily post-construction).

Hard constraints to model as timeline risk: DPD can shorten stage deadlines or deny extensions if a TIF district is nearing statutory expiration — "no exceptions" once that clock is running, so the base packet's foundational work should be complete well before a window opens in a district with a known expiration on file. Maximum of 2 extensions per stage are possible with DPD approval only for "extraordinary circumstances." A given property can't get the Maximum Program Assistance more than once every 3 years, so continuity-of-effort profiles should track prior-grant history per property, not just per applicant.

eligibility:
GEOGRAPHY: Project must sit on a designated NOF corridor on Chicago's West, Southwest, or South Sides -- either an "Eligible Corridor" (public streets generally zoned retail/commercial) or a "Priority Corridor" (zoned retail/commercial AND high existing retail/commercial activity, more competitive). Both corridor types were selected because they fall inside the Qualified Investment Area (QIA), a set of neighborhoods with sustained historic disinvestment (high unemployment/poverty/vacancy, low educational attainment). Address eligibility must be confirmed via the live NOF Eligibility Map tool (not a static list) - this is a hard, binary geographic gate that should be checked before any other packet work.
PROJECT TYPE: Must be a capital, real-estate development project = new construction, building addition, OR internal/external rehab of an existing structure (or combination). Must be revenue-generating and in substantial compliance with the Chicago Zoning Ordinance. Eligible uses: commercial (office/retail, incl. exteriors of mixed-use residential), cultural (museums/theaters/performance venues), non-profits with an on-site commercial component, artisanal manufacturing/production/services with an on-site commercial component. Ineligible: places of worship that exclusively promote religious teaching, residential/home-based/live-work uses, heavy manufacturing/industrial, social services (workforce dev, schools, daycare/elder care). Acquisition-only projects (no rehab/new construction) are ineligible.
FINANCIAL: Grant = reimbursement/escrow only, up to 75% of eligible project cost, capped at $250,000; optional Technical Assistance Fund adds up to 20% of the base grant or $50,000 (whichever less) for design/permitting/construction-management support via a DPD-approved TA provider. Applicants need proof of financing for the remaining ~50%+ of project cost; those below that threshold are diverted to a "project pipeline" (paired with a CDFI) rather than rejected outright. Total project cost must exceed $150,000 (excl. pre-development expenses) plus a 30% personal contingency to use the escrow disbursement path.
COMPETITIVE FACTORS: catalytic community impact, project readiness (site control + no material liens/court orders/past-due taxes), financial feasibility, and construction implementation readiness (GC bid quality). This is a competitive, discretionary grant, not a first-come entitlement -- DPD's final eligibility determination is discretionary even when the checklist is met.

timelineNotes: Application rounds are rolling submission, quarterly evaluation -- confirmed live deadlines: Aug 14, 2026 (current/next round) and Nov 13, 2026 (Q4); NOF states future deadlines are "subject to change and will be finalized at a later date," so cadence is stable (quarterly) but exact dates are not fixed far in advance. Selection/scoring after a deadline closes takes about 1-3 months. Once an applicant becomes a Finalist, hard internal clocks start: Stage 1 legal docs = 21 days; Stage 2 project docs (culminating in CAL) = 120 days; Stage 3 Part I proof of financing/permit = 120 days from CAL; Stage 3 Part II construction = 12 months from CAL; Stage 4 closing = 90 days from final payment request submission. Overall project completion target is 2 years from CAL (extensions require advance DPD/administrator approval or removal risk). Post-completion, a 3-year monitoring/recapture term runs from the Certificate of Completion, with annual surveys due each year -- this is the one artifact-relevant "document that expires/needs refresh" analog (recurring compliance survey, not a one-time expiring credential). Financing proof (bank statements/closing docs) is time-bound relative to CAL (must be demonstrated within 4 months of CAL), so it is a program-specific field, not something to bank indefinitely in a base profile. What CAN be prepared before a round opens / before choosing NOF as a target: geographic eligibility check via the Eligibility Map, business description/plan, entity formation and ownership documentation, site control documentation (deed/lease/purchase agreement), Sources-and-Uses / financing proof groundwork, GC bids and construction cost estimates, community-impact narrative. What CANNOT be front-loaded because it is gated by finalist/CAL status: Economic Disclosure Statement package (Stage 1, only after finalist designation), scofflaw/City-debt clearance (run per finalist), permit-in-hand and 50% financing proof verified against the specific CAL-conditioned timeline, and all draw/reimbursement documentation (only relevant after CAL, work before CAL receipt is not reimbursable at all).

eligibility:
Four Cook County Real Property Assessment Classification Ordinance incentive classes, all administered by the Cook County Assessor's Development Incentives Department with a required municipal (or County Board, if unincorporated) resolution of support:

CLASS 6b — industrial property (manufacturing, processing, recycling, wholesale distribution/storage of raw or finished goods). Triggered by new construction, substantial rehabilitation, or reoccupation of property abandoned (vacant/unused) ≥12 continuous months and purchased for value from an unrelated seller (or a municipal/County Board "special circumstances" finding of abandonment). Assessed at 10% of market value for 10 years, 15% in year 11, 20% in year 12 (vs. 25% standard industrial rate). Renewable indefinitely.

CLASS 6b SER (Sustainable Emergency Relief) — a 6b variant for an already-occupied industrial building with NO physical construction: owner must show ≥10 years of continuous same-ownership occupancy plus financial hardship/non-viability without the incentive. Heavier review chain (CCBED staff → Economic Development Advisory Committee → Cook County Board of Commissioners → Assessor). Term = 12 years or until the SER applicant vacates, whichever is sooner.

CLASS 7a — commercial projects (buying/selling or providing goods/services, incl. hotels/motels) with total development cost, excluding land, ≤$2,000,000, in an area "in need of commercial development." Requires new construction, reoccupation of property abandoned ≥24 months (shorter period possible with municipal/County Board approval), or substantial rehabilitation. Applicant must satisfy all five Sec. 74-65(a) factors: (1) area designation as blighted/conservation/renewal/empowerment zone; (2) 6-year declining/stagnant/under-realized real estate tax or AV/EAV trend; (3) project viability/timeliness; (4) assistance-and-necessity (project won't proceed without the incentive); (5) reasonably expected increase in tax revenue and employment. 12-year reduced assessment (10%/15%/20% schedule), same as 6b. Renewable.

CLASS 7b — same structure and five-factor test as 7a but for projects with development costs >$2,000,000, in an area designated "blighted" by the municipality; heavier documentation expected (pro forma financials benchmarking with/without incentive still required, but with commensurately more rigor for larger projects). Same 10%/15%/20% assessment schedule; renewable.

CLASS 8 — industrial or commercial development in areas of "severe economic stagnation": automatically eligible in Bloom, Bremen, Calumet, Rich, or Thornton townships, in a locally-certified Class 8 area, or on Cook County Tax Reactivation Project property. New construction, substantial rehabilitation, or reoccupation of abandoned property (≥24 months vacant/unused, purchase for value from unrelated seller, or special-circumstances finding). A "TEERM" supplemental track exists for abandoned property vacant 12–24 months with no purchase transaction; TEERM is NOT renewable. Standard Class 8 (non-TEERM) uses the same 10%/15%/20% schedule and is renewable.

CITY OF CHICAGO ROUTE (for property inside Chicago): before the County process can proceed, the applicant must obtain the City's ordinance of support. Since Nov. 1, 2020 (Municipal Code 2-45-160), any applicant seeking City support for a 6b/7a/7b/7c/7d/Class C tax incentive must also enter into a redevelopment agreement with the City as a condition of that support, with a substantially final version of the RDA attached to the supporting ordinance/resolution. An Economic Disclosure Statement (per County Ordinance) must also be filed with the Class 6b eligibility application. Chicago intake runs through DPD's Submittable portal (FID_Intake@cityofchicago.org, 312-744-0765), goes to the Committee on Economic, Capital and Technology Development, and requires a Community Development Commission + City Council vote before the certified ordinance/resolution can be filed with the Assessor.

timelineNotes: Hard timing trap across all four classes: the Eligibility Application (and, ideally, the municipal resolution or at least a letter that one has been requested) MUST be filed with the Assessor BEFORE construction, substantial rehabilitation, or reoccupation begins — filing after the fact makes the property ineligible. Class 6b may be filed up to (but no more than) one year before commencement. Class 7a determinations are made within 60 days of a complete filing and lapse after 1 year if the project hasn't started. Abandonment thresholds differ by class: 12 continuous months for Class 6b, 24 continuous months for 7a/7b/8 (Class 8's TEERM track bridges the 12–24 month gap for no-purchase reoccupations, but TEERM is not renewable). Triennial affidavits are strict: the Assessor mails them at each triennial reassessment and they must be signed, notarized, and returned within 3 weeks or the incentive is lost outright — no cure period. Renewal must be requested during the final year of the 10% assessment level (or while still at 15%/20%), and owners must notify the Assessor of intent to renew before requesting the municipal renewal resolution; renewal count is unlimited except TEERM. For Chicago properties, the redevelopment-agreement requirement (in effect since 11/1/2020) and Economic Disclosure Statement typically add the longest lead time in the whole pipeline, since RDA negotiation and City Council scheduling run on the City's own calendar, separate from and prior to the Assessor's township appeal deadlines (which are also independently scheduled and vary by township). What a business can prepare well in advance, independent of any specific incentive: entity/ownership documentation, PIN and site data, employment baseline figures, and (for the 7a/7b track) the 6-year tax/AV history and pro forma financial modeling, since these draw on data that doesn't change once a target incentive is chosen.

timelineNotes: Live status as of 2026-07-10, verified against official/administrator sources (not memory): SBIF is the currently active City rebate program, funded via TIF revenue, running monthly rolling application windows by TIF district through the 2026 rollout calendar (July-December 2026 cycles listed) — this is a real, open, foundation-relevant program. Chicago Workforce Solutions (successor branding to TIF-Works) is also active with Q3 (Jul 1-30, 2026) and Q4 (Oct 1-30, 2026) 2026 bond funding cycles plus year-round TIF-funded applications in 77 eligible TIF districts. On the Illinois DCEO side, the B2B and B2B-NewBiz small-business recovery grants are confirmed CLOSED (2023 application windows already lapsed) and the OE3 Small Business Capital and Infrastructure Grant is confirmed CLOSED as of April 7, 2025 with DCEO stating no plans for future funding — these should NOT be modeled as open programs in the current-cycle equivalent slot; current open DCEO small-business-adjacent items are technical-assistance/rolling programs (Small Business Development Centers, Illinois Economic Empowerment Centers, ETIP) rather than direct capital grants, so the brief's 'current-cycle equivalent' of B2B does not presently exist as an open capital grant — flag this rather than fabricate a replacement. Recency/expiry rules to encode in the foundational data model: IL good standing has no fixed statutory shelf life but program reviewers commonly want a 'recently issued' copy since it is cheap and fast to re-pull (minutes online); IDOR tax clearance requires full filing/payment compliance and cannot be obtained at all while delinquent, so it functions as a hard gate rather than a renewable artifact; City debt check similarly functions as a gate on license standing, not a document with an expiry date; EDS is the one artifact with an explicit shelf-life-like rule — drafts expire in 60 days unsubmitted, and previously-submitted non-contract data auto-expires and must be refreshed after 1 year, plus mandatory recertification before City Council action or closing on any given Matter. City is actively trying to shorten the license-standing/debt-check step via the December 2025 'Cut the Tape for Small Business' initiative, but no published new SLA yet — worth a follow-up check before hardening timeline estimates in code.
